source.title: From Text to Space: Mapping Abstract Spatial Models in LLMs during a Grid-World Navigation Task

record.tranche_reason: The study probes spatial information in a real LLM using a method different from superposition studies. It reports which individual units correlate with spatial features across prompt representations, bearing on the LLM-neuron branch of V4, but does not test superposition geometry or feature competition.
record.gate_note: The study does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity competition, or SAE features. The reported navigation success rates and comparisons among spatial formats are not rows because they do not measure a version's stated representational claim. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not rows. Rows below cover the study's unit-probing results and relevant unit ablations.
record.test_reason: The study probes LLaMA-3.1-8B hidden units for correlation with grid-world spatial features. It asks whether the representation is invariant across prompt formats, which is a world-model question. It does not measure superposition, polysemanticity, feature competition or SAE features. Its count of units correlated with a feature across all six formats measures invariance, not whether features are spread across neurons in superposition. Polysemanticity is only inferred ('likely comprised mostly of polysemantic neurons'), from an ablation that broke output coherence, and was never measured. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that spatial representations are mostly format-dependent but include abstract, format-invariant units in middle layers. Some of these are also more active on unrelated spatial questions, and they are not necessary for the simple task. The claim that spatial information sits mostly in polysemantic neurons is a hedged speculation ('likely'), drawn from the coherence-breaking ablation. It was not measured.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes LLM spatial representations and does not apply or reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The spatial information representation changes the probe results: representations generalize incompletely across SIR types, with better generalization within the same SIR class. Counts of units correlated with action correctness also vary by SIR type; Cartesian formats, especially JSON, yield the highest counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Hundreds of LLaMA-3.1-8B hidden units correlate with agent x/y position, border location and action correctness across all six prompt formats, mostly in middle layers. Units correlated with a specific grid cell across all formats: none.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLMs contain format-invariant units that track abstract spatial features (a world-model claim, not superposition).

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the 286 invariant action units barely changed success (55% vs 59%). Ablating the position units gave 62%. Ablating all JSON-correlated units (59.7% of units) destroyed output coherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Invariant spatial units are not necessary for this simple task. The authors infer, without measuring it, that spatial coding is distributed across polysemantic neurons.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code is open source on GitHub but gives no URL)
record.problems: The probing analysis focuses on one model, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and a simple 5×5 task. Unit-feature correlations do not establish that units represent clean or exclusive features; the authors note that many SIR-specific correlations may reflect input text. The cross-task analysis uses 200 spatial and 200 non-spatial questions. Ablation evidence is limited, and ablating many units disrupts output coherence.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numeric unit-count results were separately reported in text beyond R1–R5. Figure-only curves and maps were not extracted as distinct numeric rows.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
No test of capacity, importance or feature competition.
Polysemanticity is neither measured nor attributed to any cause.
Spreading of features across neurons and SAE recovery are not measured. Polysemanticity is only speculated.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The paper calls hidden-state dimensions 'parameters' and 'units'. Many single-format correlations are attributed by the authors to the input text. The superposition link exists only in the discussion's mention of polysemanticity and monosemanticity, so the study is marked as discussing the claim rather than testing it.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether importance and capacity determine dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study does not establish that polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study tests unit-level spatial correlations in one LLM and one task family; it does not test SAE recovery, other LLMs, or whether the identified units are complete features.
No SAE features or claims of canonical, complete, stable units are evaluated.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual units for significant correlation with action correctness across all six spatial information representations.
rows.measure: Number of units significantly correlated across all six SIR types
rows.note: The units were predominantly in approximately layers 12–22.
rows.check: Counts units correlated with action correctness in all six formats (286 vs 12 shuffled). This measures format-invariance of spatial coding, not V4's spreading or superposition of features across neurons. Unlink from V4.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual units for significant correlation with action correctness in at least five of the six spatial information representations.

conditions.value: at least five of six SIR types

rows.measure: Number of units meeting the significance criterion
rows.note: Most identified units were concentrated in middle layers; almost none were in earlier layers.
rows.check: Same invariance measure under a relaxed criterion (at least 5 of 6 formats). It does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual units for significant correlation with the agent's x coordinate across all spatial information representations.
rows.measure: Number of units significantly correlated across all SIR types
rows.baseline: Shuffled parameter-index control; count not stated
rows.locator: Section 5, pp. 9–10; Fig. 4, bottom second panel
rows.note: Units were predominantly in intermediate and deeper layers.
rows.check: Invariance count for agent x-coordinate units (448). It is not a measure of superposition or polysemanticity.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Tested individual units for significant correlation with the agent's y coordinate across all spatial information representations.

rows.baseline: Shuffled parameter-index control; count not stated

rows.note: Units tended to be concentrated in the most superficial layers.
rows.check: Invariance count for agent y-coordinate units (258). It is not a measure of superposition or polysemanticity.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B

rows.note: These units were primarily concentrated in approximately layers 8–18.
rows.check: Invariance count for border-cell units (373 vs shuffled). It is not a measure of superposition or polysemanticity.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Silenced the 286 units correlated with action correctness across all SIRs during navigation.
rows.note: The paper describes the performance impact as almost nil. This tests the contribution of the abstract unit group, not whether features are spread across units.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Silenced units correlated with agent position across all SIRs during navigation.
rows.note: The text says performance was not reduced but does not give the intact-model comparison value here.
rows.check: The baseline is stated in the same paragraph: 59% for the intact model (100 control trials). Ablating the position units gave 62%, so there was no drop and the state is absent, not cannot_determine.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated all units significantly correlated with action correctness for the JSON SIR.
rows.value: Model was unable to output coherent actions
rows.note: The ablated units comprised 59.7% of the total parameter count across all layers. This result concerns output coherence and does not directly test V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaMA-3.1-8B spatial features tested across the six SIR types
reader_labels.reason: The study identifies units whose activity correlates with spatial features across representations, including 286 units for action correctness and hundreds of units for position or border features (R1–R5). This supports unit-level evidence for spatial information in LLM activations, not SAE recovery or a claim of complete features.
